s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with peritonism and sepsis
salient_findings: Multi-organ involvement with lymphadenopathy and pulmonary consolidation
key_facts: 60-year-old man with history of heavy cigarette smoking
History of emphysema, hypertension, and prostate cancer in remission
Presented with 4-hour history of acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
Fever of 38.5°C on admission
Hypotensive with systolic blood pressure 90 mmHg
Tachycardic with heart rate 110/min
Peritonism in the right lower quadrant on examination
Perforated appendix with collection and surrounding fat stranding on CT
Innumerable hepatic nodules and lymphadenopathy on CT
Pulmonary consolidation and collapse in the right lower lobe on CT
Underwent exploratory laparotomy with subtotal colectomy and end ileostomy
Remained ventilated postoperatively
Failed extubation attempt on day 3
